title: Behavioral douleur échelle (BPS) pour douleur évaluation dans Intubated patients

how_to_use.why: Nonverbal patients express pain variably, making a standardized, accurate tool helpful in the evaluation of pain. Pain can be a cause of abnormal vital signs in the ICU setting, and using a quantitative tool can help confirm or refute this hypothesis.
how_to_use.when: Intubated patients, often undergoing painful procedures.
how_to_use.pearls:
- The Behavioral Pain Scale (BPS) quantifies pain using body language and patient-ventilator interactions for intubated patients.
- It was developed and validated by performing non-painful procedures (i.e., a central line dressing change) and noxious procedures (i.e., endotracheal tube suctioning) and then observing response patterns.

next_steps.advice: The BPS is a useful tool to assess pain in intubated patients.
next_steps.critical_actions: The BPS requires attentive clinical observation and examination.

more_info:
**Score interpretation:**

- Scores ≤3 indicate no pain.
- Scores 4-5 indicate mild pain.
- Scores 6-11 indicate an unacceptable amount of pain.*
- Scores ≥12 indicate maximum pain.*

***Note:** For scores ≥6 consider sedation and/or analgesia.
